title: Research Russian TTS models by size tier and gender
description: Find open-source/local Russian TTS model candidates for each requested size tier: around 100MB male/female, 250MB male/female, 500MB male/female, and 1GB male/female. For each candidate record source URL, model id/name, actual size evidence, license, runtime/format, expected CPU/GPU needs, cold-start/memory implications if available, and whether it supports dynamic load/unload in the current architecture.
design: Do not assume a model fits a tier without source-backed size evidence. Prefer engines that can be isolated behind adapters and do not require startup autoload.
acceptance_criteria: Each requested tier/gender slot has a verified candidate or an explicit evidence-backed gap; sources and licenses are recorded; candidates are ranked by integration risk; verified facts are separated from assumptions; recommended tiered shortlist is provided.
notes:
Evidence-first research result (2026-04-26): Russian local/open-weight TTS candidates by requested size/gender tier.

Current architecture constraint from repo: backend uses explicit POST /api/models/{id}/load, one loaded adapter at a time, DELETE /load unloads adapter, and current Piper adapter shells out per generation. Therefore dynamic load/unload is compatible for subprocess/ONNX adapters and possible but riskier for in-process PyTorch/NeMo/F5 adapters unless adapter.unload explicitly drops model refs and clears CUDA/MPS cache.

Source evidence and candidates:

1) Around 100 MB, male/female
- Preferred verified pair: utrobinmv/tts_ru_free_hf_vits_low_multispeaker, voices speaker_id 0 woman and 1 man. Source: https://huggingface.co/utrobinmv/tts_ru_free_hf_vits_low_multispeaker . Size evidence from HF tree: model.onnx 50,849,741 bytes; model.safetensors 60,357,152 bytes. License: Apache-2.0. Runtime/format: Transformers VitsModel or ONNX Runtime; Russian, plain lowercase text, ruaccent recommended. CPU/GPU: card shows device='cuda' or 'cpu'; ONNX path is platform-neutral. Cold start/memory: small; expect low cold start versus PyTorch heavy models, especially ONNX. Dynamic compatibility: good; can be a new onnxruntime or transformers adapter, no startup autoload required.
- Existing/alternative male: Piper ru_RU-denis-medium, ru_RU-dmitri-medium, ru_RU-ruslan-medium. Source: https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/tree/main/ru/ru_RU . Size evidence: each ONNX is 63,201,294 bytes. Licenses from model cards: denis/dmitri dataset CC0; ruslan dataset CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Runtime/format: Piper ONNX subprocess, CPU. Dynamic compatibility: already matches current piper_tts adapter. Gap: no verified safe female Piper slot with clear permissive license; irina exists at 63,201,294 bytes but model card says dataset license Unknown.
- Alternative multi-speaker: Silero v5_ru, voices aidar/eugene male and baya/kseniya/xenia female. Source: https://github.com/snakers4/silero-models and https://models.silero.ai/models/tts/ru/v5_ru.pt . Size evidence: HTTP Content-Length 145,382,211 bytes. License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Runtime: PyTorch Silero, CPU/GPU, on-demand download supported. Dynamic compatibility: possible in a PyTorch adapter; higher risk than ONNX/Piper because in-process weights must be unloaded.

2) Around 250 MB, male/female
- Evidence-backed gap for full end-to-end fixed voice models around 250 MB. Search found no fixed Russian male/female pair with source-backed model artifact near 250 MB and clear voice/gender metadata.
- Closest below, both genders: utrobinmv/tts_ru_free_hf_vits_high_multispeaker. Source: https://huggingface.co/utrobinmv/tts_ru_free_hf_vits_high_multispeaker . Size evidence: model.safetensors 159,690,732 bytes. License: Apache-2.0. Runtime: Transformers VitsModel, speaker_id 0 woman / 1 man. Gap reason: substantially below 250 MB, not a true 250 MB slot.
- Closest male-only acoustic model: bene-ges/tts_ru_ipa_fastpitch_ruslan. Source: https://huggingface.co/bene-ges/tts_ru_ipa_fastpitch_ruslan . Size evidence: tts_ru_ipa_fastpitch_ruslan.nemo 183,255,040 bytes. License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Runtime: NVIDIA NeMo FastPitch; requires IPA/G2P and separate HiFiGAN vocoder for full audio. Gap reason: not full TTS by itself; full pipeline with vocoder is ~522 MB and male-only.
- Female gap: no confirmed 250 MB female fixed Russian full TTS candidate found.

3) Around 500 MB, male/female
- Male verified full pipeline: bene-ges Russian IPA FastPitch + HiFiGAN Ruslan. Sources: https://huggingface.co/bene-ges/tts_ru_ipa_fastpitch_ruslan and https://huggingface.co/bene-ges/tts_ru_hifigan_ruslan . Size evidence: FastPitch .nemo 183,255,040 bytes + HiFiGAN .nemo 339,210,240 bytes = 522,465,280 bytes total. License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Runtime/format: NVIDIA NeMo; FastPitch takes IPA-like transcription, HiFiGAN takes mel spectrograms; G2P required. CPU/GPU: NeMo/PyTorch, practical GPU target; CPU possible only as high-latency fallback. Cold start/memory: two model loads plus G2P; materially higher than Piper/VITS ONNX. Dynamic compatibility: possible as one adapter owning both models, but unload must release both models and device memory. Integration risk high due G2P and two-stage pipeline.
- Female conditional candidate / practical-size mismatch: frappuccino/vits2_ru_natasha. Source: https://huggingface.co/frappuccino/vits2_ru_natasha and runtime repo https://github.com/shigabeev/vits2-inference . Size evidence: G_138000.pth 565,452,507 bytes; natasha.onnx 156,623,502 bytes. License: MIT. Runtime/format: card recommends vits2-inference with ONNX; model is Natasha single Russian female voice. CPU/GPU: ONNX runtime should support CPU; training card lists RTX 4090 for training only. Cold start/memory: ONNX path is moderate and much lower than 565 MB checkpoint; PyTorch checkpoint path would be heavier. Dynamic compatibility: ONNX adapter good; strict 500 MB slot is weak because the practical inference artifact is 156 MB, while the 565 MB checkpoint is not the recommended integration path.
- Female strict gap: no confirmed fixed female Russian model whose recommended runtime artifact itself is around 500 MB.

4) Around 1 GB, male/female
- Male fixed voice candidate: facebook/tts_transformer-ru-cv7_css10. Source: https://huggingface.co/facebook/tts_transformer-ru-cv7_css10 . Size evidence: model.pt 1,194,828,177 bytes plus hifigan.bin 55,825,897 bytes. License: no explicit license found in HF card/API. Runtime/format: fairseq S2 TTS + HiFiGAN, single-speaker male voice, Common Voice v7 + CSS10. CPU/GPU: fairseq/PyTorch; GPU recommended for interactive use, CPU cold start/latency likely poor. Dynamic compatibility: possible but high risk due large in-process model and missing license.
- Male/female conditional voice-clone candidate: Misha24-10/F5-TTS_RUSSIAN. Source: https://huggingface.co/Misha24-10/F5-TTS_RUSSIAN . Size evidence: inference safetensors files are 1,348,435,761 bytes; training .pt checkpoints are ~5,394,190,092 to 5,394,193,738 bytes. License: CC BY-NC 4.0. Runtime/format: F5-TTS Russian fine-tune, reference-audio voice cloning, no fixed male/female voice ids; voice identity comes from ref_audio. CPU/GPU: F5-TTS docs support PyTorch CPU/GPU installs and benchmark L20 GPU; practical interactive use should assume GPU. Cold start/memory: high; >1.3 GB weights plus tokenizer/vocoder/runtime overhead. Dynamic compatibility: possible with explicit adapter load/unload; high cold-start and GPU-memory risk.
- Alternative 1GB+ multilingual voice-clone: coqui/XTTS-v2. Source: https://huggingface.co/coqui/XTTS-v2 . Size evidence: model.pth 1,867,929,118 bytes plus dvae.pth 210,514,388 bytes and speakers_xtts.pth 7,754,818 bytes. License: Coqui Public Model License. Runtime/format: Coqui TTS XTTS-v2, supports Russian and voice cloning via speaker_wav; no fixed male/female voice id. CPU/GPU: sample uses gpu=True/use_cuda true; CPU possible but high latency. Dynamic compatibility: possible but high risk; license and repo maintenance risk higher than F5/Silero/Utrobin.
- Female fixed 1GB gap: no confirmed fixed Russian female voice around 1 GB with clear source-backed license and recommended runtime found. F5/XTTS can synthesize female only with a user-provided female reference clip, so they do not satisfy fixed voice-id female slot.

Shortlist for implementation:
- Lowest risk: utrobin low multispeaker ONNX/safetensors for both genders; Apache-2.0, one model with speaker_id 0/1, small cold start.
- Good existing-path male: Piper denis/dmitri via current piper_tts adapter; add only if license constraints are acceptable per voice.
- Best quality/noncommercial compact option: Silero v5_ru for both genders; CC BY-NC 4.0 and PyTorch adapter required.
- 500 MB male only: bene-ges Ruslan NeMo FastPitch+HiFiGAN; high integration risk due G2P and two-stage NeMo.
- 1GB conditional voice cloning: F5-TTS_RUSSIAN; only if product accepts reference-audio voices instead of fixed voice ids and GPU-heavy cold start.

Integration-risk ranking, low to high:
1. Piper ONNX subprocess: already aligned with current adapter; CPU; per-call process isolates memory.
2. Utrobin ONNX VITS: new adapter, but small artifact and clear Apache license.
3. Utrobin/Silero Transformers/PyTorch: simple model API, but in-process memory lifecycle must be implemented.
4. Frappuccino VITS2 Natasha ONNX: single female, MIT, but only fills 500 MB weakly because recommended artifact is 156 MB.
5. Bene-ges NeMo Ruslan pipeline: two models, G2P/IPA preprocessing, noncommercial license, likely GPU for acceptable latency.
6. Fairseq 1GB male: large, older fairseq stack, missing explicit license.
7. F5-TTS_RUSSIAN / XTTS-v2: voice cloning, large cold start, GPU expected, not fixed gender voice ids; license restrictions.
close_reason: Completed evidence-first Russian TTS tier/gender research with source-backed candidates, explicit gaps, shortlist, and integration-risk ranking recorded in issue notes.

title: Research 5 lightweight Russian TTS voices
description: Find at least 5 lightweight Russian TTS voice candidates suitable for local testing. Include male and female voices where available. For each candidate record source URL, model/voice id, approximate download size, license, engine/runtime, CPU feasibility, cold-start/memory notes if available, and whether it can be dynamically loaded/unloaded by the current architecture.
design:
Evidence-first research completed 2026-04-26 for lightweight local Russian TTS voices. Verified facts are separated from assumptions.

Current architecture fit:
- Verified: backend catalog entries are YAML-driven (`backend/app/catalog.py`) with adapter/runtime/config metadata; current Piper entries live in `backend/app/models/piper-russian-tts.yaml`.
- Verified: runtime loads exactly one model at a time via `POST /api/models/{id}/load`; loading another model unloads the previous adapter first; explicit unload is `DELETE /api/models/{id}/load` (`backend/app/main.py`).
- Verified: current `piper_tts` adapter is subprocess-based, checks local `.onnx` + `.onnx.json` + `piper` executable on prepare, and clears all paths/session state on unload (`backend/app/adapters/piper_tts.py`).
- Assumption: any Piper candidate below is compatible with the current architecture by adding another YAML entry using the same adapter and model/config paths; no code change should be required.
- Assumption: Silero/RHVoice candidates need new adapters, but still fit the same explicit load/unload lifecycle if adapter.prepare loads/validates local assets and adapter.unload releases in-process objects or subprocess state.

Shortlist candidates:

1. Piper ru_RU-denis-medium
- Source URL: https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/tree/main/ru/ru_RU/denis/medium
- Voice/model id: `ru_RU-denis-medium`; catalog id already present as `piper-ru-ru-denis-medium`.
- Verified size evidence: HF API reports `ru_RU-denis-medium.onnx` size 63,201,294 bytes plus `ru_RU-denis-medium.onnx.json` size 4,823 bytes. Approx total 60.28 MiB.
- Verified license evidence: model card says dataset URL `https://github.com/OHF-Voice/voice-datasets`, License `CC0`.
- Engine/runtime: Piper, ONNX + JSON, subprocess CLI in current app; PyPI `piper-tts` 1.4.2 reports GPL-3.0-or-later; OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl GitHub API reports GPL-3.0.
- CPU feasibility: verified Piper describes itself as fast/local; current app hardware notes say CPU/no GPU. Assumption: good CPU candidate for local testing.
- Cold-start/memory notes: verified no upstream memory numbers found in primary source during this pass. Assumption: cold start is mostly subprocess launch + ONNX load per request in current adapter, because generation invokes `piper` per turn.
- Dynamic load/unload compatibility: verified compatible now; existing adapter checks paths/executable on load and clears state on unload.
- Recommendation: include in default lightweight set.

2. Piper ru_RU-dmitri-medium
- Source URL: https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/tree/main/ru/ru_RU/dmitri/medium
- Voice/model id: `ru_RU-dmitri-medium`; catalog id already present as `piper-ru-ru-dmitri-medium`.
- Verified size evidence: HF API reports ONNX 63,201,294 bytes plus JSON 4,824 bytes. Approx total 60.28 MiB.
- Verified license evidence: model card says dataset URL `https://github.com/OHF-Voice/voice-datasets`, License `CC0`.
- Engine/runtime: Piper, ONNX + JSON, subprocess CLI in current app; runtime GPL-3.0/GPL-3.0-or-later evidence as above.
- CPU feasibility: same as Denis.
- Cold-start/memory notes: same as Denis; no primary memory numbers found.
- Dynamic load/unload compatibility: verified compatible now.
- Recommendation: include in default lightweight set.

3. Piper ru_RU-irina-medium
- Source URL: https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/tree/main/ru/ru_RU/irina/medium
- Voice/model id: `ru_RU-irina-medium`.
- Verified size evidence: HF API reports ONNX 63,201,294 bytes plus JSON 4,765 bytes. Approx total 60.28 MiB.
- Verified license evidence: model card says dataset URL `https://github.com/RHVoice/RHVoice`, License `Unknown`.
- Engine/runtime: Piper, ONNX + JSON, subprocess CLI with existing adapter pattern.
- CPU feasibility: same Piper CPU/local assumptions as Denis.
- Cold-start/memory notes: same as Denis; no primary memory numbers found.
- Dynamic load/unload compatibility: assumed compatible with current Piper adapter via YAML-only catalog entry.
- Recommendation: best female-sounding lightweight Piper candidate for internal/local tests only; do not make production/default distributable until dataset/model license is resolved.
